caption: Fourteen months left on a loan I took out just to get through the divorce. Would you have done it differently?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R27 500
p/m salary
Living in George
slides.body:
Male, 34
Single dad, one son (7) lives with him full time
Job: Diesel mechanic, logistics depot
Net salary: R27 500 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 2 bed in Blanco, needed the extra room once he moved in with me full time
slides.body: One bedroom would have been cheaper. It wasn't really an option.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: Bakkie, needed something reliable once I was doing school runs alone
slides.body: Can't be the parent whose car doesn't start on a Monday.

slides.title: Personal loan
slides.includes: R21 000 taken out for legal fees during the custody process, 14 months left
slides.body: I don't love that a custody fight is still costing me monthly. I'd do it again.

slides.title: Groceries & school lunches
slides.includes: Shoprite run, plus the lunchbox stuff that runs out faster than the trolley suggests
slides.body: He's seven. He eats like he's seventeen.

slides.title: Aftercare & school fees
slides.includes: Aftercare until I'm off shift, plus the school's extras
slides.body: The aftercare bill is basically a second rent.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, electricity, phone, insurance, funeral policy, savings, and the loan interest on top of the instalment
slides.body: This is where the loan actually bites — the interest is buried in here, not in the line above.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R27 500. Once the loan's done in fourteen months this gets a lot less tight.

slides.title: I stopped ignoring the loan repayment date
slides.body:
I added the personal loan to Beyond Horizon's debt tracker and watched the payoff date for the first time.

Fourteen months left. Seeing it counted down made it feel like it's actually ending.

No bank login needed.
